loop.top3_series_pattern: trend_dominated, high predictability, weak seasonality, non-stationary
loop.top3_why: The series is strongly trend‑dominated and the model rankings are moderately stable (Kendall tau ≈0.69). A selective strategy that averages only the most consistently ranked models is therefore appropriate. Candidate A uses a trimmed‑mean over pool3 (9 models) which balances robustness against the limited number of validation windows and mitigates the risk of overfitting that a single best‑model approach (candidate C) would incur. Its per‑window performance is consistently good across all three windows, whereas the best‑single strategy shows a large drop in window 1, indicating potential overfitting to the other windows.
loop.top3_why_not: Candidate B trims a smaller pool (5 models) and, while still stable, offers less diversity than pool3, potentially reducing robustness. Candidate C relies on a single model (DWT_rf) that is not the best in all windows; its large error in window 1 suggests it may not generalize well to the blind test period. Thus A provides the best trade‑off between stability and performance.
